On MMLU, SGLang can reuse the KV cache of the 5-shot examples with RadixAttention. RadixAt-
tention benefits both throughput and latency. RadixAttention reduces total memory usage by sharing
the KV cache, allowing for a larger batch size to improve maximum throughput. RadixAttention
also reduces the computation of prefill, thus decreasing the first token latency. On HellaSwag,
SGLang reuses the KV cache of both few-shot examples and the common question prefix for multiple
choices, resulting in two-level sharing. For the ReAct and generative agents, SGLang reuses the
KV cache of the agent template and previous calls. On Tree-of-thought and Skeleton-of-thought,
SGLang parallelizes the generation calls within a single program and reuses the KV cache as much
as possible. On JSON decoding, SGLang accelerates decoding by decoding multiple tokens at once
with a compressed finite state machine. In multi-turn chat, SGLang reuses the KV cache of the chat
history. The speedup is more noticeable for short outputs because KV cache reuse mostly helps
reduce the prefix time. For long outputs, because there is not much sharing between different chat
sessions and the decoding time dominates, there is almost no speedup. In the DSPy RAG pipeline,
SGLang reuses the KV cache of the common context example. On these benchmarks, the cache hit
rate ranges from 50% to 99%. Fig. 13 (Appendix) lists the achieved and optimal cache hit rates for all
of them, showing that our cache-aware scheduling approaches 96% of the optimal hit rate on average.
We exclude LMQL and Guidance from some of the last five benchmarks due to slow performance and
missing functionalities. LMQL’s issues stem from slow token-level processing and an unoptimized
backend, while Guidance lacks batching and parallelism support.
Results on larger models with tensor parallelism. We run larger models, Mixtral-8x7B and Llama-
70B, with tensor parallelism on the same set of benchmarks and report the results in Fig. 7 and Fig. 12
(Appendix). The speedup on larger models shows a trend similar to that observed on smaller models,
indicating that our optimization generalizes well to larger models. We omit Guidance and LMQL
here because they lack efficient implementations of tensor parallelism.
Results on multi-modal models. SGLang has native support for multi-modal models with the
image and video primitives. The optimizations in this paper are compatible with multi-modal
models. For RadixAttention, we compute the hash of the input images and use it as the key in the
radix tree, allowing us to reuse the KV cache of the image tokens from the same image. We run
LLaVA-v1.5-7B (image) on llava-bench-in-the-wild and LLaVA-NeXT-34B (video) on ActivityNet.
Because these models are not well supported by other baseline systems, we use the model authors’
original implementation in Hugging Face Transformers as the baseline. As shown in Table 2, SGLang
provides throughput up to 6× higher on these benchmarks. In llava-bench-in-the-wild, there are
multiple questions about the same image, and SGLang runtime reuses the KV cache in this case.
Production deployment. SGLang has been deployed in Chatbot Arena [8] to serve open-weight
models. Due to low traffic for some models, only one SGLang worker serves each. After one
month, we observed a 52.4% RadixAttention cache hit rate for LLaVA-Next-34B [28] and 74.1% for
Vicuna-33B [7]. Cache hits come from common system messages, frequently reused example images,
and multi-turn chat histories. This reduces first-token latency by an average of 1.7× for Vicuna-33B.

Results on API models. We test a prompt that extracts three fields from a Wikipedia page using
OpenAI’s GPT-3.5 model. By using few-shot prompting, the accuracy of API speculative execution

6.3
Ablation Study
Cache hit rate vs. latency/throughput. Fig. 8(a)(b) shows the relationship between cache hit
rate and performance metrics (first token latency, total latency, batch size, and throughput) on the
tree-of-thought benchmark. The figure is obtained by partially disabling matched tokens at runtime.
It shows that a higher cache hit rate leads to a larger batch size, higher throughput, and lower latency.
Effectiveness of RadixAttention. We test the effectiveness of RadixAttention and its components
on several representative benchmarks. As shown in Fig. 8(c), "No Cache" means not using any
cache, "No Tree-Structure" means using a simple table-based cache instead of a tree-structured cache,
"FCFS Schedule" means using a first-come-first-serve policy instead of our cache-aware scheduling,
"Random Schedule" means using a random order to schedule requests, "No Frontend Parallelism"
means disabling parallelism in the interpreter, "No Frontend Hint" means disabling sending the
fork hints from the interpreters, and "Full optimizations" means we turn on all optimizations. The
experimental results show that each of these components is required to achieve the best performance.
Disabling parallelism and hints from the frontend interpreter also results in suboptimal runtime
performance, highlighting the importance of co-designing the frontend language and runtime.
Overhead of RadixAttention. We test the overhead of RadixAttention on a benchmark without any
KV cache reuse opportunities. The benchmark measures throughput on the ShareGPT dataset. It
takes 74.3 seconds to run 100 requests; however, the time used for managing the RadixAttention data
structures is only 0.2 seconds, which is a negligible overhead of less than 0.3%. This is because the
complexity of tree operations is linear and small. Thus, we can turn on RadixAttention by default.
Effectiveness of the compressed finite state machine. We test the effectiveness of the compressed
finite state machine and its components on the JSON decoding benchmark. Experimental results
show that the compressed finite state machine increases the throughput by 1.6× because it can decode
multiple tokens at once. In addition, we need to preprocess the state machine and reuse it for a batch
of requests. Otherwise, redoing the preprocessing for each request makes the throughput 2.4× lower.
7
Related Work
Various works have explored the reuse of the KV cache, and many of them are concurrent with our
work. Uniquely, our RadixAttention first proposes treating the KV cache as a tree-based LRU cache.
It is the first solution that supports multi-level sharing, cache-aware scheduling, frontend-runtime
co-scheduling, and distributed cases. vLLM [23] and ChunkedAttention [58] explore some simple
reuse cases (e.g., system prompt sharing) but do not cover multi-level tree-structured sharing or LRU
caching. PromptCache [12] proposes the modular reuse of the KV cache beyond the prefix but can
impact accuracy by up to a 43% drop. HydraGen [18], FlashInfer [59], and ChunkedAttention [58]
focus on CUDA kernel optimizations and do not include the concept of an LRU cache. API Serve [1]
and LLM-SQL [29] study KV cache reuse for specific applications such as interleaving with external
API calls and relational databases, but they do not have our radix tree or cache-aware scheduling.

Several LLM programming and agent frameworks exist, such as Guidance [13], LMQL [4],
DSPy [20], LangChain [24], AutoGen [55], and LLM Compiler [21]. Guidance and LMQL are most
similar to SGLang, and we compare them in Sec. 2. Our innovation lies in novel runtime optimizations
for accelerating the proposed programming model. SGLang is compatible with other frameworks and
can accelerate them (e.g., the DSPy example in our evaluation). Additionally, SGLang is compatible
with many other common inference optimizations [60, 39, 3, 23, 59, 10, 26, 15, 19, 32, 31, 11].
8
Future Directions and Conclusion
Future directions. Despite the progress made with SGLang, several limitations remain that reveal
promising directions for future research. These include extending SGLang to support additional
output modalities, adapting RadixAttention to operate across multiple levels of the memory hierarchy
(e.g., DRAM, Disk) [43], enabling fuzzy semantic matching within RadixAttention, providing higher-
level primitives atop SGLang, fixing starvation in cache-aware scheduling [42], and enhancing the
SGLang compiler to perform advanced static optimizations such as scheduling and memory planning.
Conclusion. We introduce SGLang, a framework for efficient programming and executing structured
language model programs. SGLang significantly improves the throughput and latency of complex
LM programs through novel optimizations like RadixAttention, compressed finite state machines,
and a language interpreter. It is a valuable tool for developing advanced prompting techniques and
agent workflows. The source code is publicly available.

A
Additional Details on RadixAttention
A.1
Background on the KV Cache
Most LLMs in use today, such as GPT-3 [5], PaLM [9], and LLaMA [49], are based on the autore-
gressive Transformer architecture [51]. These models predict the probability of the next token in a
sequence based on the preceding tokens. During inference, the model first processes a sequence of
input tokens through a forward pass (this process is called "prefill"). It then sequentially decodes
output tokens, with each token depending on prior tokens (this process is called "decoding"). We
refer to the process of taking a sequence of input tokens and generating a sequence of output tokens
as a single-generation call. Throughout this process, each token generates some intermediate tensors,
which are used for decoding further tokens. These intermediate tensors, known as the "KV Cache,"
are named for the key-value pairs in the self-attention mechanism. An important observation when
discussing optimizations in this paper is that the computation of the KV cache only depends on all
previous tokens, so different sequences with the same prefix can reuse the KV cache of the prefix
tokens and avoid redundant computation.
Often in LLM programs, multiple text segments and generation calls are appended to a single
prompt. Caching the computed KV cache for previous tokens across multiple chained calls can
reduce redundant computation. This optimization, however, is neither free nor trivial, as it requires

like irregular tree-structured sharing can also be employed. Fig. 9 shows four typical patterns of KV
cache sharing across multiple calls; none of the existing systems can automatically handle all of them.

Next, we show that the longest-shared-prefix-first order is equivalent to a DFS order by induction.
• (Base) In the beginning, since there is nothing cached, a random request that corresponds to
a node x in T will be processed. All requests that correspond to the nodes {v1, ..., vn} on the
path from the root to x do not need a recomputation. The computation complexity for requests
corresponding to the nodes {v1, ..., vn, x} is aligned with a valid DFS. The path from the root to
x is cached.
• (Induction) Assume we just visited a node y in T, and the visited nodes align with a DFS order.
Let P denote the path from the root to y. Then each node that has not been visited has the lowest
common ancestor with the visited nodes on P. Since nodes on P are cached, a node z that has
not been visited with the lowest common ancestor on P will have the longest shared prefix. The
longest-shared-prefix-first order will select z, which is a valid DFS order. The path from the root
to z will be cached because it is the most recent.
In the online case, the DFS order will be disrupted, but the longest shared prefix schedule still
approximates the DFS behavior on the augmented part of the implied radix tree. We show this by
considering the step of adding a new batch of requests.
Let T denote the part of the radix tree that has been visited so far, and T ′ denote the whole new
radix tree after adding the new batch of requests. Let C denote the set of cached nodes in T. Let
longest(C) denote the node in C that has the longest path from the root and has a subtree in T ′ that
has not been fully visited.
The longest shared prefix schedule will then process the subtree in T ′ rooted at longest(C) in a DFS
order. During this process, eviction could occur, and the remaining cached nodes from C become
C(1) ⊆C. A DFS will then occur for the subtree in T ′ rooted at longest(C(1)).
Similarly, we will have C(2), . . . , C(k), until C(k) contains only one leaf node in C(k) that has its

A.4
Data-Parallel Distributed RadixAttention
To adapt the RadixAttention for distributed settings with multiple replica workers (i.e., data par-
allelism), we developed a mechanism wherein each worker maintains its own sub-tree, while the
router oversees a meta-tree. This meta-tree acts as a trie that tracks all sub-trees and their associated
devices. Upon the arrival of a new batch of requests at the router, prefix matching is executed on the
meta-tree. We implement various policies based on each request’s affinity—measured by the length
of the shared prefix with specific workers and other requests in the same group—to make efficient
dispatch decisions that minimize redundant computations. Each time new requests are processed,
both the router and workers independently update their respective trees. Should an eviction occur
at a worker node, it commits this eviction to a queue, which the router then processes to update the
meta-tree during periods of low activity. We benchmarked this distributed configuration using four
workers and the MMLU dataset, observing that it achieves linear scaling and an optimal cache hit rate
with minimal overhead from this weakly consistent distributed cache design. There exists a trade-off
between maximizing data locality and parallel processing efficiency. Exploring advanced scheduling
policies to optimize this trade-off is designated as an area for future research. In addition, concurrent
work from Preble [45] studies data-parallel scheduling based on an early version of SGLang.

The challenge of constrained decoding arises from the fact that constraints are often expressed in
natural language formats, i.e., regex is depicted by characters/strings, while LLMs are designed to
interpret and process these as tokens. This creates a complex scenario since the mapping between
strings and tokens is intricate and lacks a one-to-one correspondence [22].
This section is derived from an earlier blog post4. Readers are also encouraged to read the blog post
for additional background and easier understanding.
B.1
Implementation Details of Compressed Finite State Machine
To simplify the construction of Compressed FSM, we build the original FSM on characters/strings
instead of on tokens. We formally define the concepts of singular transition edge and compressed
edge as follows:
• Singular transition edge: A edge is a singular transition edge if 1) its source node has only one
successor node, and 2) there is only one acceptable character/string on it.
• Compressed edge: An edge compressed by several consecutively adjacent edges (e0, e1, . . . , ek)
if and only if e1, . . . , ek are singular transition edges. The text of the compressed edge is the
concatenation of the texts of e0, e1, . . . , ek.
Starting from an FSM based on characters, we recursively merge singular transition edges into
their preceding ones until further compression is unfeasible, resulting in a Compressed FSM. This
approach speeds up the decoding process, as demonstrated by SGLang’s runtime efficiency with the
Compressed FSM, shown in Fig. 11.
B.2
Handling Tokenization Artifacts with Retokenization
When a new token is generated, we get the token’s string and search all the outgoing edges of the
current state find the one that starts with the just decoded string, and then move forward. However,
when the transition edge is a well-compressed one and contains a very long string, we may anticipate
the next rounds’ decoded strings as well. This is where the acceleration happens and we call this
process Jump Forward. However, we still need to convert the string into tokens for the next decoding
phases and it is not straightforward due to the LLM’s specific pretraining and tokenization method;

The challenge caused by the gap between strings and tokens also brings the problem of skewed proba-

issue of distorted probabilities, highlighting the need for further research to improve the compressed

D.1
Design and Implementation
We designed an intermediate representation (IR) for SGLang, which represents SGLang program
structures and operations as a computational graph. This graph includes nodes for primitive operators
and edges for dependencies. See Fig. 14b for the graph corresponding to the program in Fig. 14a. In
the program, each call to a decorated function or fork creates a new prompt state or a stream.
There are several types of nodes. Each operand of the operators += and + in a SGLang program
is represented by an IR node. These include ConstantText, Argument, Gen, Select, Variable,
Fork, GetForkItem, and Join. There are two types of dependencies: intra-stream dependency,
where operations submitted into a stream using += must be executed after all preceding operations
in that stream, and inter-stream dependency, which occurs when one stream needs to fetch variable
values from another stream, necessitating synchronization. Operations like fork manipulate multiple
streams and thus introduce inter-stream dependencies.
To generate the graph, we use tracing to run the program with abstract arguments and construct
the graph dynamically. This method is limited to programs without data-dependent control flow, a
limitation we plan to address in future work. Once constructed, the graph can be executed through
a graph executor, eliminating the need to reinterpret the original Python program. This results in
benefits like graph rewriting optimizations, reduced runtime overhead, and program serialization. For
execution, stream executors are launched for each data stream, dispatching IR nodes to the streams in
topological order.
D.2
A Case Study of Compiler Optimization: Code Movement for Improving Prefix Sharing
We explore a compilation optimization for SGLang IR: code movement for improving prefix sharing.
We anticipate that more classical compiler techniques can also be applied, such as auto-tuning and
instruction selection.
This optimization aims to improve prefix sharing by reordering nodes in the graph to increase the
length of the constant prefix. It does not strictly preserve the original computation, classifying it as
an aggressive optimization. For instance, changing the prompt from “Here is a question + {question}.
Please act as a math expert and solve the given question.” to “Please act as a math expert and solve
the given question. Here is a question + {question}.” results in a longer shareable prefix. This
optimization is interesting because traditional program analysis cannot achieve it due to the presence
of natural language instructions in SGLang. Instead, we prompt GPT-4 to reorder graph nodes. We
write a prompt with several examples to teach GPT-4 the concepts of SGLang IR, and we find that
GPT-4 can successfully apply this optimization for some simple SGLang programs.

def gradual_select(dev, mandatory_by_layer, sizes):
  n=len(dev[0])
  S=set(range(n))
  out=[S]
  for i in range(1,len(sizes)):
    M=mandatory_by_layer[i]
    if not M <= S: raise ValueError
    need=sizes[i]-len(M)
    cand=sorted((j for j in S if j not in M), key=lambda j:(-dev[i-1][j], j))
    if need<0 or len(cand)<need: raise ValueError
    S=set(M)|set(cand[:need])
    out.append(S)
  return out
```

{"chapter":"# K-ALG-022：非前缀上下文复用：依赖、位置与选择性重算

同一段文本在两个请求中出现，只能证明输入内容重复。对因果 decoder，位置 t 的第 i 层状态还取决于可见前缀、位置规则、模型与 adapter 版本，以及实际数值格式。非前缀复用的设计起点，是把这些依赖写成可检查的对象，再决定哪些状态可以精确搬移、哪些只能用选择性重算逼近。

## 依赖闭包：同文本不等于同状态

设一次前向的条件为 η，包括模型与权重版本、tokenizer 与规范化、adapter、位置编码参数、可见性规则、dtype 与量化格式。已知 token 序列记为 x[0:N)，位置 t 的第 i 层状态记为 S_t^i。对普通因果 decoder，S_t^i 是 η 与可见前缀的函数；滑动窗口、递归状态或跨片段 mask 也必须进入 η，不能用普通全历史的公式替代。

因此缓存的逻辑对象不是一个文本串，而是某个条件下完成到位置 p 的状态。前缀缓存可以复用 S(η,x[0:p))，因为后续 token 没有进入这个前缀的计算图。非前缀片段 B 放在 A 后面时，B 的第一层投影最初仍可能只看到 B 的 embedding 与位置，但经过 attention 后，B 的隐藏状态已经吸收 A 的可见信息；更深层的 B K/V 因而依赖 A。把 B 改到 C 后面，即使 B 的 token 和位置相同，逐层状态仍可能变化。

需要分开三个目标。第一是完整函数的数值一致或逐位一致；第二是给定表示与算术契约下的误差界；第三是任务质量达到阈值。选择性重算通常只属于第三类或带质量条件的第二类。少数任务上回答相同，不能升级为任意输入的精确复用。

输入至少包含请求身份、η、片段及版本序列、每段 token 的绝对位置与目标位置、缓存层次与就绪范围、查询或未命中位置、允许的重算比例。输出应给出恢复位置或融合后的私有状态、每层选择集合、就绪与所有权，以及失败标记。已分配、已加载、已转换、部分更新完成、消费者可见是不同状态，不能用一个命中长度代替。

## 合法性：精确、位置变换与近似

精确前缀复用的条件是 η 相同、token 序列相同、位置与窗口规则相同、状态表示相同，并且所需层和范围都已就绪。若某层只保存窗口状态，或另存递归检查点，恢复位置必须落在所有状态族共同允许的位置集合中；最大长度相近不等于可跳过长度相同。

若模型明确规定片段间互不可见，独立片段的 KV 才可能按该可见性直接组合。这个条件必须由参考函数本身满足；人为关闭跨片段 attention 会改变模型函数，不能作为原模型精确复用的实现技巧。完整 KV reuse 若忽略跨片段 attention，只能作为近似候选，并以任务质量验证。

RoPE 提供的是位置坐标的旋转关系，不是上文依赖的恢复。把每个二维通道对写成旋转矩阵，

R(pθ)=[[cos(pθ),-sin(pθ)],[sin(pθ),cos(pθ)]],
R_{Θ,p}=blockdiag(R(pθ_1),…,R(pθ_{d/2})).

若旋转前的 K 向量确实相同，旧位置 p 的状态可以转到新位置 p′：

K_{p′}=R_{Θ,p′}R_{Θ,p}^{T}K_p。

对位置 a 的 query 和位置 b 的 key，完整旋转满足 q_a^T K_b=q^T R_{Θ,b-a}k，因此相对位置内积由完整旋转矩阵保证。频率、缩放、旋转维度、通道配对布局和位置缩放必须一致；绝对位置 embedding 或其他位置变换需要重新建立对应条件。

二维反例可以直接检查实现是否漏掉交叉项。令 q=(1,0)、k=(0,1)，q 旋转 π/2 后为 (0,1)，k 保持角度 0，点积为 1；若只把各分量乘以 cos(π/2)，q 变成 (0,0)，点积变成 0。这个错误在只看单个向量的范数或只看同维乘积时可能被掩盖。

| 路线 | 需要的条件 | 能保证什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 精确前缀复用 | η、完整前缀、位置、状态与格式一致 | 同一后续计算的精确状态，浮点逐位一致仍需单独声明 |
| 独立片段组合 | 参考模型确实隔离片段可见性 | 该隔离函数下的精确组合 |
| RoPE 位置搬移 | 旋转前 K 相同，频率与布局一致 | 只修正位置坐标，不补跨片段 attention |
| 选择性重算 | 有可读取缓存、在线选择规则、质量阈值 | 允许误差或任务质量下的近似 |
| 全 KV reuse | 跨片段 attention 可忽略或已声明为近似 | 需要端到端质量验证，不能称原函数精确 |

## 选择性重算：从缓存到当前输入

CacheBlend 固定 v1 的机制是逐层做部分更新：只对一部分 token 重新计算当前层的 Q/K/V，把新 K/V 写入对应逻辑位置，其余位置沿用缓存；被选中的 Q 与该层完整可见 K/V 做 attention，得到下一层需要的隐藏状态。这样能减少被选中 token 的投影、MLP 和 attention 行计算，但全历史 K/V 的读取、装载和索引仍然存在。

选择集合必须来自在线可取得的信息。一个可执行实例先在首层完整计算或计算一个探测区域，得到新旧 K/V 偏差，再在后续层逐层缩小集合。使用所有层完整重算得到的偏差来选 token 属于离线 oracle，只能评价选择策略上限。首层尚未吸收上文时，不能假定它已经暴露深层跨片段偏差。

```pseudocode
输入：请求身份 req、条件 η、片段序列、查询与未命中位置、每层缓存 K/V 与就绪状态、强制集合 M、选择规模计划 k_i
输出：私有 fused KV、每层选择集合 S_i、就绪状态，或明确失败

核对 η、tokenizer、位置参数、可见性、dtype、层范围与租约；不合法则拒绝
令 C 为命中缓存的片段位置，Q 为查询和未命中位置；M 必须包含 Q 与产生最终 logits 的行
令 S_1 为 C 与 Q 的并集；建立私有 fused 层数组与必要读租约
对 i=1…H_l：
    等待第 i 层缓存完整到达、转换完成且对消费者可见；核对句柄代次和范围
    对 j∈S_i 取得第 i 层隐藏输入 h_i[j]；首层用 embedding，否则用上一层为 j 计算的输出
    只对 j∈S_i 计算新的 Q_i[j]、K_i[j]、V_i[j]
    在私有 fused 层 i 中，j∈S_i 用新 K/V，j∈C\S_i 用缓存 K/V，Q 全用新 K/V
    对 j∈S_i 的 query 与所有合法可见 K/V 做整体 softmax 与 PV
    对 j∈S_i 应用该层剩余 MLP、残差与 norm，得到 h_{i+1}[j]
    若 i<H_l：
        对 j∈S_i∩C 计算新 K/V 与旧缓存的偏差 d_i[j]
        令 S_{i+1}⊆S_i，强制集合 M_{i+1}⊆S_{i+1}
        在 S_i 中按 d_i 从大到小选至多 k_{i+1} 个位置；已丢弃位置不得无输入重新加入
全部层完成后，在私有区提交 fused 快照与查询 logits
失败或取消：不发布部分快照；停止新增工作，等待已提交读写结束后释放私有范围
```

不变量包括：S_{i+1}⊆S_i；M 在每层都存在；被丢弃 token 没有新的隐藏输入时不能重新扩张；每层 fused K/V 的逻辑位置与可见性固定；消费者只能读取已完成层。若把 S_i 取为全部位置，算法退化为完整 prefill，可作为同一实现的全量参考。

查询文本、未命中的新片段和必须产生最终输出的 token 应放入强制集合，不能被缓存命中比例掩盖。若最终输出依赖末行 logits，而这些 logits 没有随缓存保存，就必须安全重算相应末端，不能只恢复 KV 后直接采样。重算写区必须私有或经过证明的写入隔离，不能覆盖仍被其他请求共享的命中页。

首层全算再逐层缩小是论文背景中的一种安排，不是唯一合法算法。也可以先算探测区域，或按层组观察偏差；但任何安排都要保持 S_{i+1} 的输入依赖，并说明选择规则使用了哪些在线信息。偏差阈值、层间衰减和重算比例是模型与任务相关参数，不是知识库常数。

## 状态、所有权与发布

公共片段缓存与某次请求融合后的缓存是不同对象。公共对象应保持其原始依赖含义，例如片段版本、token 范围、位置策略和表示格式；融合结果还依赖前序片段顺序、目标位置、选择集合和当前代次。将融合结果覆盖回公共片段 B，会污染后续请求。修改部分应使用私有缓冲、写时复制或显式组合条目。

请求状态至少包含片段版本序列、各片段 token 范围、原位置与目标位置、每层就绪范围、重算选择集合、数值格式、私有页代次与取消资格。公共缓存项可以有 READY、LOADING、FAILED、DRAINING 等生命周期；私有 fused 页在提交前不可被消费者读取。加载完成、位置变换完成、部分更新完成、消费者可见是不同事件。

共享物理页只有在逻辑引用与物理读者都结束后才可复用。目录中的逻辑引用计数不能替代异步读完成；取消后要停止新增工作，并等待已经提交的读写结束。迟到完成必须按原请求、原对象和原代次结算，不能覆盖新分配的页。若融合结果需要长期保存，应为其建立包含片段顺序与选择策略的新身份，而不是沿用独立片段身份。

KV 量化、裁剪与片段融合的误差不能分别通过后直接视为组合通过。量化会改变偏差排序，裁剪会删除融合需要访问的位置，稀疏页布局会改变 gather 成本。近似缓存应沿用其构建策略身份，避免精确前缀路径误读它。

## 成本：计算、加载、流水与驻留

设总材料长为 L，第 i 层重算 r_i 个 query。投影、MLP 和被选中 query 的 attention 行大致随 r_i 增长；对全历史 K/V 的读取、装载和索引仍可能与 L 相关。选择、gather/scatter、位置变换、缓存解码、尾块浪费和不规则 kernel 的效率都要另计。因此重算 10% token 不等于耗时 10%，尤其当加载或索引占主导时。

若把每层加载时间记为 a、计算时间记为 c，共有 H_l 层，加载与计算使用独立资源且有足够缓冲，理想流水时间为

T=a+c+(H_l−1)max(a,c)。

设定 H_l=4、a=6 ms、c=2 ms，得到 26 ms，串行为 32 ms；若 c 增为 9 ms，流水为 42 ms，串行为 60 ms。此时计算不能被 6 ms 的加载隐藏。实际还要加入启动、尾部、选择和竞争开销；若加载与计算共享 HBM、PCIe 或设备队列，a、c 必须在并发条件下测量，不能把两个独占测量值直接代入。

设一层完整 attention 的时间为 A，投影与 MLP 合计为 P，完整层时间为 A+P。若选择性重算把某一部分计算降到比例 r，而未减少的加载与固定准备占时间为 F，则大致有 T_selective≈F+r(A+P)。即使 A+P 很大，只要 F 成为瓶颈，继续降低 r 也不会等比例缩短端到端时间。用 Amdahl 形式估算，若可缩减部分占完整计算 70%、比例降到 0.15，计算加速约为 1/(0.3+0.105)=2.47 倍，不能写成 1/0.15。

容量也不能用命中片段数乘一个常数。对普通全 attention，每 token 全层 KV 的逻辑字节为

B_KV=H_l L H_kv (d_K+d_V) s，

K 与 V 同宽时写成 2H_l L H_kv d s。这里 H_kv 是 KV head 数，不是 query head 数；TP/PP 产生物理副本时要按落点相乘。另有格式元数据、页尾、私有更新、位置转换、双缓冲与选择索引。设 H_l=32、L=8192、H_kv=8、d=128、s=2，则每个完整序列约 1 GiB；若只有 3072 个缓存 token，则约 384 MiB，尚未计私有融合页和元数据。

驻留容量按实际物理分配求并集，不能把公共缓存、请求映射和传输缓冲各算一份。多个组合若要分别保存融合结果，复用率上升可能伴随容量急剧增加；需要比较保存独立片段后近似融合，与保存少数常用完整前缀。

## 条件变化、反例与方案反转

| 条件变化 | 保留的关系 | 调整或放弃的依据 |
|---|---|---|
| 前缀完全命中且 η 不变 | 精确前缀复用成立 | 继续检查末行 logits 与共享写区 |
| 相同片段换到不同前序 | 片段文本相同但深层状态依赖改变 | 不能精确复用；改用选择性重算或完整 prefill |
| RoPE 只改变目标位置 | 旋转前向量与频率一致时可搬移坐标 | 跨片段 attention 仍未恢复，质量仍需验证 |
| adapter、模型版本或位置缩放改变 | 旧缓存身份失效 | 隔离、重算或建立新身份 |
| 长材料、跨片段依赖强 | 选择性重算可能有收益 | 若质量不达标，提高重算范围或回到完整函数 |
| 缓存加载很慢、重算很快 | 加载是瓶颈，选择性重算可能被隐藏 | 比较完整 prefill、缓存加载与排队，不只比较命中率 |
| 高精度答案或罕见实体依赖 | 近似误差可能改变结果 | 扩大强制集合或放弃近似复用 |
| KV 量化或裁剪改变偏差排序 | 旧选择策略失效 | 重新校准选择规则并组合验证质量 |

精确前缀命中高、材料很短或设备重算很快时，常规前缀缓存与全量 prefill 更有利。长材料的非前缀复用高、传输可以与少量重算重叠且质量阈值允许时，选择性重算才可能获益。跨材料依赖强、查询分布变化或高精度答案要求提高时，应提高重算范围或回到完整函数。决定反转的信号是端到端成本与质量约束，而不是缓存命中率本身。

论文报告的经验重算比例来自其模型、数据与评估设置，不能成为本章默认保证。片段长度、顺序、查询分布、位置规则和数值格式改变后，偏差排序与质量阈值都要重新验证。

## 区分实验与验证边界

先建立完整 prefill 参考，固定材料文本、顺序、查询、模型、adapter 和采样设置。覆盖 A→B 与 C→B、A→B 与 B→A、同文本不同位置、一个字的否定修改、跨片段指代、不同 adapter、缺失缓存以及加载中断。记录逐层 K/V 偏差、最终 logits 偏差，同时在真实任务上测答案正确性、依据一致性和长材料表现。

竞争解释要用可控改变区分。高命中率而 TTFT 未改善，至少有三种解释：命中长度不等于共同可恢复长度；命中避免了计算却引入传输、转换或排队；命中已正确生效，但新 query 对长历史的 attention 或查询后缀仍占主要时间。分别记录逻辑匹配、实际跳过位置、完成计算 token 数、加载时间、选择时间、部分更新时间和最终查询时间。

选择性重算的质量对照应固定总预算，比较随机选择、按 KV 偏差选择、离线 oracle 和完整重算。若随机选择与偏差选择给出相同结果，当前选择信号不能解释收益；若逐层偏差改善而任务质量不改善，偏差指标不足以代表任务重要性。负对照包括强制丢弃查询 token、让选择集合在下层无输入地重新扩张、提前发布部分层，以及把公共片段缓存覆盖为融合结果。

RoPE 检查应分别验证完整二维旋转、位置搬移等式和相对内积。只把各分量乘以 cos 的错误实现应在二维反例中失败；只比较单向量范数不能替代旋转关系。完整旋转矩阵、频率和通道配对固定后，再用同一 query 检查旧位置与新位置的点积关系。

性能统计包含检索后到首输出的全部阶段；若声明用户端 TTFT，还须包含检索和重排。固定 p 比较本地与远端、固定路由比较只读缓存与冷启动、改变 suffix 长度并保持前缀相同，可以区分前置准备、加载、选择、融合计算和最终查询各自的影响。

本章检查脚本只执行确定性的 CPU 软件模型，验证二维旋转与位置搬移、选择集合嵌套和强制集合、容量公式、流水时序以及所有权隔离；它不执行真实 GPU kernel，不测 HBM 带宽、缓存一致性、任务质量或 Agent 使用效果。论文中的数值与本章设定算例均不能替代目标设备测量。
